spiritual_reading:
The text is too fragmentary to yield a fully coherent continuous spiritual narrative. Much of the sequence, the agents, and the predicates are lost, so several motions of influx and several subjects resist translation. What follows is the most faithful spiritual rendering possible from the surviving clauses, with uncertainties where the missing words prevent a determinate sense.

Within the Divine realm of wisdom there is a distinct state in which truth shines from good and all things are seen from that shining.

In a supreme degree of that same realm, the Divine intends to disclose higher things, and whatever is disclosed there is disclosed from what is prior and interior.

In that interior degree, perception is alive because it receives life from the Divine, and the living presence that proceeds from the Divine rests upon the recipient and gives it form and vitality.

From the shining of wisdom and from the living presence, an outflow goes forth that renders what is within intelligible and apparent. There is then a sufficient series of consecrated powers for worship and acknowledgment, gathered into the living delight of good. These sufficient powers are joined into one operative whole, so that together they present a single spiritual form, and within that form the breath of life is living, and its activity is living.

When those sufficient powers are brought through every opposition that arises in the process of establishing greatness, they are conjoined into a beautiful unity. What proceeds from that unity is joined to every faculty of the whole person, so that the entire organized spiritual person exists in the realm of wisdom; and from that conjunction there is life in each part.

As every heavenly and spiritual community, and every abundance of good and truth, and every ministry that is called into function, proceeds from the Divine Itself, so also every elevation of state, every rising of interior truth, and every perception that bears uses, proceeds from the same source and continuously flows forth. Great is the Divine in this: that everything that is is sustained by what proceeds from the Divine, and nothing is truly living from itself; neither understanding without love, nor love without understanding, nor any effect without an interior source.

These things are the ordered realities of that realm, though the specific series intended here is unclear because the text is missing.

There is a further degree—its place in the sequence is uncertain—in which wisdom in fullness and the living breath of heaven are the common atmosphere of life; within this, the higher states of greatness dwell as established forms. There are ministering powers there who carry out their functions, and there are the gifts that proceed from the Divine, received and distributed in orderly ways within that realm; the remaining particulars are unclear because the predicates are lost.

Blessed is the one who comes into knowledge of these things, because such knowledge is not mere awareness but reception, conjunction, and life.

fills.fill: The Father established all things in
fills.notes: Opening needs a cosmological subject that can be implied in ¶6 (“came from the Father”) and leads naturally into “the Land of Light.” Old substrate prefers impersonal cosmogonic statement of establishment rather than exhortation.
Gives a simple subject for the self-report style that survives (“as I will reveal to you”), without importing later dialogic frame.
Completes “great land of greatness … as I will reveal to you” with a disclosure-term. The following “above” suggests a promised exposition of the mode or order.
Balances “reveal to you” and anticipates “above” (interior, prior). Keeps structural register: things set or established in the higher degree.

Produces “surface” as the natural term that corresponds to outward perception. The fragment “[ ... f]ace” strongly constrains to “face,” but “surface” better fits correspondential move to what shines forth.
Needed to construe the clause: “surface is … living …”.
Restores “proceeding” to match the spiritual sense “presence that proceeds from the Divine.”
The agent “upon him” requires a source; ¶6 explicitly names “the Father.” Oldest layer uses “Father” as principle of Light rather than Christian person-title.
Introduces the outflow described: “From … light and … face … out”.
Links “light” and “face” to the same subject implied in ¶3–4.
Fits “face … out; he has …” with an emanation verb consistent with influx-outflow logic.
Again yields “surface/face,” keeping the same term-pattern as ¶3. The repetition suggests a technical term in the substrate.
“face of the … in the …” is best as “of the greatness,” echoing “land of greatness” and “aeons of greatness.”
Provides the receptacle/location: “in the aeons,” matching ¶8 explicitly (“aeons of greatness dwell”).
“now five … of praise” suggests fivefold powers as rays or lights; “rays” coheres with ‘light’ and later ‘image’.
Completes “praise” to “praise” with visible letters; minimal restoration.
“in the … living ambrosia” needs a container-term: place/region. Keeps cosmological geography register.
Bridges “living ambrosia … five … compound …”: locates the five within the delight-substance; maintains impersonal descriptive tone.
The spiritual translation identifies “a sufficient series of consecrated powers.” “Five powers” is the tightest old-layer term without later ecclesial language.
Makes “five … compound … they become an image” coherent: the five are compounded together.
Connects compounding to result: “so that they become an image …”.
Produces “living” with the fixed l + i + v + ing letters around it.

fills.fill: and the breath within it is
fills.notes: Prepares “the living air … also living” by specifying the inner breath as the living air. Correspondentially: breath as life proceeding within the formed image.
The spiritual sense speaks of being brought through opposition/contests; the old-layer natural expression is purification/refinement through struggle.
Matches “from all the contests,” giving the completion of the process before unity/beauty is mentioned.
Supplies what “a beautiful …” points to in the spiritual rendering (“beautiful unity”).
Completes “which” in “[ ... w]hich”.

fills.fill: as an image of the great Man
fills.notes: “to the limbs of their body … which exists … land of light” strongly suggests the Primal Man archetype. This is substrate-cosmic anthropology, not moral exhortation.
Makes “exists in the land of light;” coherent.
Completes “their … life” with a dependence statement consistent with ¶6 (“nothing … from itself”).
Balances the series “mountains … springs and trees …” with an inclusive coordinator.

fills.fill: that are set in their places
fills.notes: Makes the cosmological list structural rather than scenic: elevations, springs, trees as ordered states/uses.
Matches the repeated doctrine of procession: all gush forth from the Father/source.
“great is a … every thing” needs a noun like wonder/marvel; keeps impersonal admiration of order.
Completes “everything that you … neither water nor …” as an epistemic claim: “that you see”.
Pairs naturally with “water” as complementary elements; correspondentially understanding and love, or truth and good in ultimates.
Completes “These ar[e … ]” to “are”.
Supplies the missing predicate: ordered realities fixed by measure, matching the spiritual translation’s “ordered realities… series”.
A “-th” degree is referenced; “third” is a plausible sequence marker without forcing later systematics. Confidence limited because numbering is not preserved.
Completes “The …-th … great light,” with “degree” matching spiritual rendering (“further degree”).
Grammatical bridge to “great light, the living air …”.
Restores the function of angels in this layer: ministering powers carrying out ordered uses, not devotional guardians.
The plural is already supplied by the surrounding “angel[s]”; no extra letter required beyond the editor’s bracket, but the listed lacuna requires an entry. Best is to supply nothing substantive.
Fits “angel[s] that … and the …”: they stand or are stationed in that atmosphere as established forms.
Prepares “the gifts of the great Father” with a repository-term used in cosmogonic descriptions: treasures, storehouses.
Completes “gifts” with fixed letters.
Connects gifts to reception/distribution implied by the spiritual translation.
Closes “in the …” with the realm-name appropriate to this degree; maintains parallel with “aeons of greatness” and “Land of Light.”
Completes “k[now ...” as “know these things,” aligning with the concluding beatitude in the spiritual translation.

assessment: Most gaps can be restored at the level of cosmological logic: procession from the Father, fivefold powers forming a single image, life as breath within the formed image, and the doctrine that nothing lives from itself. Exact phrasing and any original ordinal numbering in ¶8 remain the loosest points; several small connectors are necessarily tentative because the Coptic-English surface syntax is too broken to constrain them more tightly.
